Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs - post-call recap

Thanks again for the time today - good conversation. Quick recap from our discovery + a few follow-ups so we can scope a dedicated-capacity validation run that demonstrates the SLOs you care about.

Recap of requirements we captured:
- Latency SLOs: p95 generation latency target <= 150 ms for non-streamed requests; streaming partial-token latency target <= 80-100 ms for first-byte/partial outputs.
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state ~120 req/s, hourly spikes up to ~400 req/s for ~20-40s, sustained burst tolerance to ~600 req/s for short windows. Peak concurrent in-flight requests ~30-50.
- Model: Llama-3-70B (quantized FP16/int8 variant) with ~512 token context and avg response length ~120 tokens.
- Streaming: client displays partial tokens as they are generated; need consistent <100 ms first-byte latency during stream.
- Availability/SLAs: prediction reliability during spikes, automated fallback to smaller model if we hit capacity.

Open items / asks for the validation run:
1) Confirmation of token length distribution and any extreme tail cases (e.g., >1024 tokens) - Carlos, can you share a sample distribution or a small anonymized dataset?
2) Agree on validation window (we suggested a 4-hour ramp test with intentional spike pattern). Proposed dates: Mar 24-25.
3) Prioritized metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency, throughput sustained vs burst, concurrency, CPU/GPU utilization, and generation token-per-second.
4) Budget guardrails: any upper bound we should avoid exceeding during test (so we can size reserved throughput conservatively).

Next steps (proposed):
- Aditya will propose GPU sizing options (A100 vs H100) and reserved-throughput sizing based on the workload.
- We'll share a validation-run plan and a short quote for dedicated capacity.
- If you approve, we schedule a 4-hour validation run during your off-peak window.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf (high level sizing + assumptions), validation-run-plan.xlsx (test pattern + metrics we'll collect).

Thanks - I'll keep this short. Please reply with the token distribution and whether Mar 24 or 25 works.

--Marissa

Following up with a technical sizing note based on the workload you described and our internal benchmarks. High level recommendations and trade-offs below.

Assumptions: Llama-3-70B quantized FP16/int8 serving, 512 context, avg output 120 tokens, batching <= 8 for low-latency traffic, streaming enabled.

GPU comparisons (ballpark, per single-GPU serving of that model):
- NVIDIA A100 40GB (optimized kernels, quantized):
  - Estimated steady throughput: ~140 req/s (single-stream, optimized runtime)
  - p95 latency (single-request, low batching): ~140-180 ms
  - Best for cost-conscious commitments; more GPUs needed for headroom.
- NVIDIA H100 80GB (sparser kernels, faster FP16 paths):
  - Estimated steady throughput: ~210-260 req/s
  - p95 latency: ~90-130 ms
  - Better performance for streaming and lower p95 with similar batch sizes.

Sizing guidance (to meet your SLOs: p95 <=150 ms, streaming first-byte <=100 ms):
- Recommendation A (H100-first): Start with 3 H100-equivalent cards reserved for Dedicated (gives ~630-780 req/s headroom), leave autoscaling burst enabled for transient >800 req/s. This matches your spike profile and keeps p95 under target with modest batching.
- Recommendation B (A100-first): Start with 5 A100-equivalent cards reserved (~700 req/s total) to provide similar throughput but expect slightly higher p95 and more variability during bursts.
- If extreme-tail long responses (>=900 tokens) are a material % of traffic, we recommend isolating those onto a separate pool with larger context configs to avoid impacting small/fast requests.

Autoscaling notes: Redwood Dedicated supports fast vertical scaling + burst pools, but to guarantee strict p95 during the hourly spike we recommend reserving a baseline (as above) and allowing burst autoscaling as insurance. Autoscaling adds a short warmup (tens of seconds); we can configure a warm standby pool to reduce warmup.

Cost delta (very rough): H100 reserved capacity ~25-30% higher monthly commit vs equivalent A100 capacity, but fewer cards needed and better p95. We'll include a more detailed quote in the official doc.

Validation run plan (we'll execute per the attached validation-run-plan.xlsx):
- 4-hour window (Mar 24, 13:00-17:00 PT) with controlled ramp and scheduled bursts: 120 req/s steady -> 400 req/s hourly spike -> 600 req/s short burst injections.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, token-per-second, streaming first-byte latency.
- Success criteria: p95 <=150ms for non-streamed; streaming first-byte <=100ms for >=95% of streaming requests during spikes.

I attached a short sizing doc (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf) and the test pattern workbook (validation-run-plan.xlsx). If you can share the token-length distribution, we'll plug that into our simulator and produce an updated per-GPU throughput estimate before the run.

Let me know if you want us to run the validation against your data in a dedicated staging VPC (we can arrange a secure ingest flow) or against a synthetic workload that mirrors your distribution.
